identity.name: Sayyid dynasty
alt_names: Sayyid Dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate

land.text: Delhi and its surroundings, taken from Daulat Khan Lodi, who held the city after the last Tughlaqs

predecessors.note: 'On 28 May 1414, Khizr Khan captured Delhi and imprisoned Daulat Khan Lodi' (Khizr Khan page). The Tughlaq dossier dates the entry 6 June 1414.

land.text: Delhi, the Sayyid realm handed to Bahlul Lodi by Alam Shah's abdication

successors.note: 'Ala-ud-Din voluntarily abdicated the throne of the Delhi Sultanate in favour of Bahlul Khan Lodi on 19 April 1451' (infobox 20 April 1451).

rulers.name: Khizr Khan
rulers.note: Took no sultan's title and kept nominal allegiance to the Timurids; died 20 May 1421.

rulers.name: Muhammad Shah
rulers.note: The text gives 1434-1443 and his death in 1445.

correction.text: the 1415 shape extended back to 1414, with Multan

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's row begins in 1415, but Khizr Khan 'captured Delhi on 28 May 1414, thereby establishing the Sayyid dynasty' (infobox 'established 28 May 1414'). 88,975 km2 (bbox 74.6-78.9 E, 26.5-29.5 N) for the Cliopatria shape; the page gives no area. Multan (71.4 E) is not in the shape; Khizr Khan governed it from 1398 and it passed to his family (Khizr Khan page), so it is added (repair 2026-10-20: it was a 1414 gain from the Timurids, now part of the founding land).

correction.text: the 1415 shape plus Multan, years 1415 only

keyframe_review.note: Years 1415 only (the shape is split at July 1416, when Bayana and Gwalior are annexed). 88,975 km2 (bbox 74.6-78.9 E, 26.5-29.5 N) for the Cliopatria shape; the page gives no area. Multan, the fief of Abdur Rahman, is added back until the Langah seizure of 1445 (ledger). Bayana lies inside the shape.

correction.text: the 1415 shape plus Multan and Gwalior

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Taj-ul-Mulk's army 'was sent to Bayana and Gwalior ... and annexed both the regions' in July 1416 (Khizr Khan page). Bayana is inside the 1415 shape; Gwalior (26.2 N, below the shape's 26.5 N edge) is added, with Multan, to 1444. The ledger's Bayana radius adds nothing new.

correction.text: the 1415 shape plus Gwalior, without Multan

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Multan goes to the Langahs in 1445 ('In 1445, Rai Sahra ... attacked the city', Langah page; ledger). The Sayyid page's reign bound for Muhammad Shah is 1443, the Langah page's year 1445; the later year is used so that both dossiers agree. The shape holds to 1449.

correction.text: the 1450 shape plus Gwalior, years 1450-1451 only

keyframe_review.note: Years 1450-1451 only: the page has the dynasty end on 20 April 1451, so Cliopatria's 1452 year is dropped. Gwalior is kept to the end and goes to the Tomars in 1451 (bridge, ledger). Multan is gone (Langahs); Bahlul Lodi, governor of Sirhind, 'gradually gathered enough power to attack Delhi' (Sayyid page).

ledger.note: 1414: Katehar pays tribute. An army under Taj-ul-Mulk suppressed the revolt of Har Singh, Raja of Katehar, 'who eventually surrendered and agreed to pay tribute'.

region.text: Delhi and its surroundings, with Multan, Khizr Khan's own governorship

ledger.note: 28 May 1414: Khizr Khan takes Delhi and founds the Sayyid dynasty. 'He then captured Delhi on 28 May 1414, thereby establishing the Sayyid dynasty.' He did not take the title of sultan and kept a nominal allegiance to the Timurids (see the vassal_start below). Repair 2026-10-20: Multan is part of the founding land, not a gain: Timur appointed Khizr Khan 'deputy of Multan' in 1398 with charge of Lahore, Dipalpur, Multan and upper Sindh (Sayyid page) and he governed Multan from 17 December 1398 to 28 May 1414 (Khizr Khan page); after Delhi 'Abdur Rahman received Multan and Fatehpur'. Lahore and Dipalpur are not kept: no page opened says they stayed with the Sayyids. The counterpart is the Tughlaq dynasty for Delhi.

region.text: the Sayyid realm and Multan, as a Timurid vassal

ledger.note: 28 May 1414: the Sayyids hold Delhi as Timurid vassals. Khizr Khan 'continued the fiction of his allegiance to Timurids as Rayat-i-Ala' and took no royal title (Sayyid page); he 'continued to pay [Timur] tribute' and in 1417 'obtained permission from Shah Rukh to have his own name also suffixed to that of Shah Rukh' (Khizr Khan page, as the reviewer quotes it). Recorded from the vassal's side (repair 2026-10-20: the first version left it to the Timurid dossier). Confidence 2: the pages give the relation, 1414 is the founding year, the land is the Sayyid shape. The timurid-empire dossier has no mirror yet.

July 1416: Bayana and Gwalior annexed. Taj-ul-Mulk's army 'was sent to Bayana and Gwalior ... and annexed both the regions'. The page names no ruler of either, so the counterpart is the chiefs of the two places.
1418: 'Har Singh rebelled again but was decisively defeated by Taj-ul-Mulk.' The page does not say whether tribute was resumed; the tributary relation is closed at the rebellion.

1421: the allegiance is dropped, a bridge. The Sayyid page says 'Mubarak Shah discontinued his father's nominal allegiance to Timur' (reign 1421-1434) without a year; the Mubarak Shah page says he 'received a robe and a chatr ... from the Timurid capital of Herat, which indicates that the fealty continued in his time' (undated). The pages disagree; 1421, the start of his reign, is the earliest year the Sayyid page's sentence allows. Mirrors timurid-empire (to be added).

1445: Multan passes to the Langahs. 'In 1445, Rai Sahra, chief of the Langah, attacked the city at night with the help of his tribesmen' and 'arrested Sheikh Yousaf and proclaimed himself sultan' (Langah page, infobox 'Established: 1445'). The Sayyid page says only that 'Multan became independent under the Langahs during [Muhammad Shah's] rule', which it dates 1434-1443 in the infobox and by his death 'in the year 1445' in the text. Repair 2026-10-20: moved from 1443 (a reign bound) to 1445 so as to match langah-sultanate /ledger/0 (found 1445, confidence 3). The Langah page also has the inhabitants choosing Shaikh Yousaf as ruler 'in 1438' and the city 'independent of the Sultanate of Delhi' after Timur's invasion, so Delhi's hold may have lapsed earlier; the year here is the Langah seizure, with the Sayyids shown holding the fief until it. Confidence 2: year from the Langah page, the Sayyid hold to that year is a reading.

April 1451 at the latest: Gwalior is no longer the Sayyids', a bridge. The Khizr Khan page has Bayana and Gwalior 'annexed' in July 1416; no page opened says how long the hold lasted. The Lodi dossier has the Tomars of Gwalior as Gwalior's rulers in 1500 (Sikandar Lodi page) and takes it in 1518, so the land cannot pass to Bahlul Lodi in 1451. Added so that the 1416 gain does not leave Gwalior without an owner at the dissolve (repair 2026-10-20).

19/20 April 1451: Alam Shah abdicates to Bahlul Lodi. 'Ala-ud-Din voluntarily abdicated the throne of the Delhi Sultanate in favour of Bahlul Khan Lodi on 19 April 1451'; he retired to Badaun, where he died in 1478.

wars.name: Katehar campaigns
wars.outcome: Har Singh surrendered and agreed to pay tribute in 1414; he rebelled again and was decisively defeated by Taj-ul-Mulk in 1418.

wars.name: Annexation of Bayana and Gwalior
wars.outcome: Taj-ul-Mulk's army was sent in July 1416 and annexed both regions.

wars.name: Sayyid-Malwa war
wars.outcome: Mubarak Shah defeated 'the advancing Hoshang Shah Ghori, the ruler of the Malwa Sultanate' and forced him to pay tribute (page gives the span 1421-1434). No border moved.

wars.name: Sharqi invasion of Delhi
wars.outcome: Ibrahim Shah Sharqi 'annexed large parts of the Delhi Sultanate and besieged Delhi'; Muhammad Shah 'sought for peace and offered a matrimonial alliance', his daughter Bibi Raji marrying Ibrahim's son Mahmud Khan. The page names no place taken and no border afterwards, so the ledger records no change (repair 2026-10-20).

certainty.note: No treaty line or survey is recorded on the pages opened; the realm is Delhi, the Doab towns and fiefs, and its limits are approximate. Multan is a governor's fief until 1445; the Timurid fealty is nominal (ledger).

sources.title: Sayyid dynasty
sources.note: Identity, dates (28 May 1414 to 20 April 1451), rulers, Malwa war, Langahs, Timurid allegiance (Khizr Khan 'continued the fiction of his allegiance to Timurids as Rayat-i-Ala'; Mubarak Shah 'discontinued his father's nominal allegiance to Timur'), Muhammad Shah 'died in the year 1445'. No area on the page.

sources.title: Khizr Khan
sources.note: Delhi capture, Katehar, Bayana and Gwalior 1416, Multan fief, Shah Rukh 1417.

sources.title: Mubarak Shah (Sayyid dynasty)
sources.note: Reign 1421-1434; the Timurid fealty continued (robe and chatr from Herat); no mention of Multan, Lahore or Jaunpur (repair 2026-10-20).

sources.title: Langah Sultanate
sources.note: 1445: Rai Sahra seizes Multan; 1438: the inhabitants chose Shaikh Yousaf (repair 2026-10-20).

sources.title: Ibrahim Shah Sharqi
sources.note: 1437 war on Muhammad Shah of Delhi; 1406-1407 campaigns against Mahmud (Tughlaq time); reign 1401-1440 (repair 2026-10-20).

notes:
Cliopatria rows: two shapes 1415-1452, identical area (88,975 km2). The page has the dynasty from 28 May 1414 to 20 April 1451 (month 5 against the Tughlaq dossier's 6 June 1414 for Khizr Khan's entry); the shapes are extended back to 1414 and cut at 1451.
Not settled: the Sayyid realm's extent is not described on either page (Doab, Mewat, Etawah, Kanauj, Punjab and the Jaunpur wars are not mentioned); the shape of record is kept for Delhi proper and corrected only for Multan (which it lacks) and Gwalior (annexed 1416).
Timurid vassalage is now in the ledger (repair 2026-10-20): vassal_start 1414 (Sayyid page, 'Rayat-i-Ala'; Khizr Khan page, Shah Rukh's name on the coinage in 1417) and a confidence-1 vassal_end 1421. The Sayyid page has Mubarak Shah dropping the allegiance; the Mubarak Shah page has him receiving a robe and chatr from Herat, 'which indicates that the fealty continued'. No year on either; the pages disagree and the end year is a bridge. The timurid-empire dossier (ia-02) has no matching vassal_start/vassal_end yet.
Multan: folded into the founding land (found event and 1414 keyframe) instead of a 1414 gain from the Timurids; the 1443 loss is moved to 1445 to match langah-sultanate. Disagreement kept: the Langah page has the inhabitants choosing Shaikh Yousaf in 1438 and Multan independent of Delhi after Timur's invasion; the Sayyid page puts the Langah independence in Muhammad Shah's reign (1434-1443 infobox, died 1445 in the text).
Gwalior: the 1416 annexation has a confidence-1 loss to the Tomars at the end of the dynasty (1451) so that the land does not pass to Bahlul Lodi; the Lodi dossier takes Gwalior from the Tomars in 1518.
Still thin: the Sayyid realm's extent (Doab, Mewat, Etawah, Lahore, Dipalpur) is not described on the Sayyid, Khizr Khan or Mubarak Shah pages; the Sayyid-Jaunpur wars are recorded only for 1437 (Ibrahim Shah Sharqi page: he 'annexed large parts of the Delhi Sultanate and besieged Delhi'; no place named, so no ledger event); the 1433 siege of Mahmudabad (Kalpi) is not recorded. Page budget (2) used: Sayyid dynasty and Khizr Khan; repair added Mubarak Shah (Sayyid dynasty) and Langah Sultanate.
Gazetteer: Bayana is not in the gazetteer (lon/lat used).
